notes: Step 1 parts were correct; no parts added or dropped.

The breadboard uses the catalogue naming: bank 't' is rows a-e and bank 'b' is rows f-j. In the image the half with rows f-j is at the top and the half with rows a-e is at the bottom, so those rows map to banks 'b' and 't' respectively.

The image draws the bottom rails as an upper black (negative) row and a lower red (positive) row. They are named bn.<n> (ground) and bp.<n> (5V). Rail hole numbers are approximate, taken from each wire's x position.

The button straddles the centre gap in columns 4 and 6. Column 4 is side 1 (1.l top, 1.r bottom) and column 6 is side 2 (2.l top, 2.r bottom). The catalogue joins 1.l with 1.r and 2.l with 2.r inside the part. Which of l/r is top or bottom is an assumption.

Orange wire: column 4 (button side 1) to the 5V rail. Teal wire: pin 2 to column 6 (button side 2). The 10k pull-down resistor runs from column 6 to column 9, and the short black wire takes column 9 to the ground rail. So pin 2 sits on the same side as the pull-down resistor, and the other side goes to 5V.
The black wire from the Arduino goes to the second GND pin on the power header, so I used GND.2. The red wire goes to 5V.
The built-in LED on pin 13 is on the board, so there is no external LED.
